clue.text: Scold when coming in at minimum speed?

indicators.note: a word coming in enters another word and sits inside it

blocks.note: to scold is to berate
as in 'as he left' means when he left

explanation.surface: A telling-off delivered while crawling along at the slowest speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scold' looks like the definition, but the answer is a financial term and the question mark stretches it to a speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A base rate is the lowest standard level of a charge or pace, so the question mark lets it stand for a minimum speed.

clue.text: See 20
Fire with wine

blocks.note: first meaning: to dismiss from a job
second meaning: an old name for dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: A fire fed with wine, or wine served by the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is the wine Falstaff drinks in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to sack them, and sack was the Elizabethan name for imported sherry-like wine.

clue.text: Flexible games

blocks.note: first meaning: the stretchy material, used as an adjective
second meaning: a set of games in bridge or whist

explanation.surface: Games that can bend to suit the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'games' is a plural noun, but a rubber is a single set made up of several games.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber describes bendy, elastic things, and in bridge or cricket a rubber is a series of games played as one match.

clue.text: Majority once at county? None in this puzzle? Oh yes there is!

definitions.text: None in this puzzle? Oh yes there is!
definitions.note: a comment on the grid: there is no clue numbered 21 down, except this answer itself

blocks.note: twenty-one was the age of coming of age before it was lowered to eighteen
County Down is in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A pantomime exchange about whether a coming-of-age party is missing from the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 21 in this grid is an across light only, so there is no clue 21 down; 'Oh yes there is!' is the pantomime reply, since this answer spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid has numbered lights, and the setter jokes that the one missing number is supplied by this very answer.

clue.text: County administrators?

blocks.note: first meaning: the short form of Staffordshire, an English Midlands county
second meaning: bodies of employees who run an organisation

explanation.surface: The officials who run a county council.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest local government officers; apart they are two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs is the postal abbreviation of Staffordshire, and the staffs of offices are their employed workforces.

clue.text: Means of altering shape

indicators.note: the following word is the material that, put through a process of change, produces the result

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tool or method for changing a figure's form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' does double duty in the surface as the act of change, but it is simply the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided figure, one of the basic geometric shapes.

clue.text: Join the ranks, giant eating liver, etc - it's easy

definitions.note: the phrase is used as 'as easy as falling off a log'

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself, so one piece is swallowed by the other

blocks.note: the military order to line up in ranks is 'fall in'
Gog is one of the legendary giants, paired with Magog
liver, kidneys and the like are offal

explanation.surface: A recruit lines up while a giant chews offal, and it all seems simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are the legendary giants whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall; the swallowed offal reads as three words once inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as easy as falling off a log needs no effort at all, the idiom for a very simple task.

clue.text: Saint and devil allowed to fly back without breaking ties - it's easy

definitions.note: the phrase is used as a description: it is simplicity itself

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start
something broken is smashed apart and its parts end up in a new arrangement
in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
an imp is a little devil
licit means lawful, allowed
taken as written
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A saint and a devil are allowed to fly home without their ties coming apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: the reversed YLF wraps round the shuffled ITSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is simplicity itself means it could not be easier, a fixed idiom for a trivial task.

clue.text: Welcome interruption by Pole to relieve embarrassment?

blocks.note: N stands for the North Pole
breaking the ice relieves awkwardness at a first meeting

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor's interruption that eases an awkward silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the compass pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause from work or routine that is pleasant to have is a nice break, so a welcome interruption.

clue.text: Cook's ideal - variegated film, always changing colour

indicators.note: variegated means patched with varied colours, so the letters come out mixed and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a pic is a slang word for a film or photograph

explanation.surface: A chef's dream is a colourful, ever-changing film.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope's patterns shift colour with every turn, so kaleidoscopic describes something constantly varying in hue.

clue.text: I'm a severe critic of religion

blocks.note: the speaker, the subject of 'I am'
to be a severe critic of something is to slam it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a harsh critic of a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'I slam': being a severe critic of something means slamming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded on the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Very tiresome model in quiet island surrounded by bells

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it
what is surrounded sits within the outer word

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
quiet means silent
I is the abbreviation for island
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A model stuck on a quiet island ringed by church bells.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford is a standard crossword source for a lone T; the island letter follows the quiet word before both go inside the bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilential literally means plague-like, and colloquially describes someone or something extremely annoying.

clue.text: River with aquatic mammal and tailless wader - so I was there all along!

definitions.text: so I was there all along!

indicators.note: without a tail, so the final letter of the bird's name is dropped

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a seal is a sea-going mammal
an ibis is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: A riverside wildlife scene that ends in a suspect's sudden confession.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is what a detective, or a suspect caught out, says when a claimed absence collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: When a claimed absence from the scene of a crime turns out untrue, the suspect was present the whole time.

clue.text: Certificates? I issue one shortly, if directed

indicators.note: directed as in stage-managed, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
one of the certificates, cut short to its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: An official explains that they will issue a brief certificate when instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points back to the first word: one certificate, shortened, is a cert.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks and bonds are traded as securities, each represented by a certificate of ownership.

clue.text: Top copy by 10

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a top copy of item ten.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10-down, but it is just the number in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, its very summit.

clue.text: Coco oil is grand treatment, contextual rather than personal

indicators.note: a treatment works something over, so these letters are processed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A beauty salon's coconut-oil treatment that works on everyone rather than the individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociologic explanations look to society and social setting rather than the individual's own psychology.

clue.text: Comprehensive expression of disapproval about heroin

indicators.note: one word goes round another, which sits within it

blocks.note: a catcall is a whistle or jeer of disapproval
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A thorough telling-off over somebody's drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all term or clause covers every case, so it is all-embracing and wide in scope.

clue.text: Dachshund gets the treatment at a party - droop around

indicators.note: the last word goes around the rest, which ends up inside it

blocks.note: to droop is to sag
usage is the way something is treated
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A long-bodied pet is fussed over at a party and wilts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'droop' sounds like a description of the tired dog, but SAG is the outer shell for the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage dog is the affectionate British nickname for the long, short-legged German breed.

clue.text: The right size for furious reaction

blocks.note: first meaning: clothes that are a good fit
second meaning

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage over getting the right size.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that suits your measurements is a fit, and an outburst of temper is also a fit, as in having one.

clue.text: How Oberon said he could raise some money?

definitions.text: How Oberon said he could raise some money?

blocks.note: surface reading: the fairy king's famous line in A Midsummer Night's Dream, about a slope where wild thyme grows
setter's reading: the speaker has a contact at a financial institution who might lend him cash

explanation.walkthrough: Oberon's speech begins with the line about a flowery slope; read as everyday speech, it is a boast about access to a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of Shakespeare's line, taken literally, are what someone hoping for a loan might say.

clue.text: Each round number in forgery is easy

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: apiece means each
the letter O is round
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a forgery is a fake

explanation.surface: Forging every round number is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a piece of cake is idiomatically very simple to do, needing little effort.

clue.text: See 7
In the centre of some of the world's wonders

indicators.note: only part of the word is wanted, so its outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: the Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the Seven Wonders of the World

explanation.surface: Standing at the heart of one of the ancient world's marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: The wonders must first be named before part of the word is taken; drop PYR and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of or surrounded by something.

clue.text: I have business on an island

blocks.note: taken as written
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone has work to do on a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, famous for nightlife.

clue.text: Amateur, then, with some blemishes is easy

indicators.note: only part of the following word is wanted, so its tail is dropped

blocks.note: an amateur is no pro
taken as written, before its ending is cut

explanation.surface: An amateur with a few skin blemishes finds it no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no problem means it presents no difficulty, the same as saying a task is easy.

clue.text: See 8
Capitals that are small and untidy should be throttled

blocks.note: SC is the printer's abbreviation for small capitals
ragged means scruffy, untidy

explanation.surface: A typographer fumes that whoever set untidy small capitals deserves strangling.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is a typesetting mark meaning small capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrag someone is to wring their neck, so scragged means seized by the throat and strangled.
